34837:
Tidewater Rock

Tidewater Rock is a fortified tower over 70 feet tall built on the rocky shore of Windward Isle. It is made of sturdy masonry walls atop a 10-foot-high stone base, filled with packed dirt. A stone stair rises to the heavy front door. Tidewater Rock sits right on the lagoon's edge and commands a good view of almost the entire island. At high tide, the water rises almost to the height of its stone base. The current owner of the Rock is Agasta Smythee, widow of the pirate Iron Bert Smythee.⁠
5664697:
Stoneclimb

Stoneclimb is a fortress along the eastern side of the Icerime Peaks in Brevoy. It is south of Skywatch and it is in the north of lands controlled by House Medvyed and from where that House lives and rules.⁠
9678607:
Anjing

Anjing is a city located in the southeastern Heisong Forest of the Successor State of Lingshen.⁠ Anjing is a vast metropolis, its inhabitants numbering over sixty thousand.⁠

According to legends, Anjing was the site of one of the challenges of the Tian Xia zodiac hero Tian Shen. Tales say the mythical hero lost an archery challenge due to his opponent's aggressive taunting, leading him to spend months mastering and balancing his qi through the practice of qigong. Tian Shen won the rematch through his renewed focus by striking the bullseye with every shot, each perfectly splitting his previous arrow. The constellation of the Archer is said to depict this event.⁠
24263487:
Veshtak

Veshtak is a small town on the Marbleflow River in the Irriseni province of Wintercrux. The town is in a strategic location where the merchants load their cargo onto ships traveling the river north.⁠

Veshtak won the right to govern itself a generation ago, using bribes and political connections. The town exploits its position by exacting high tariffs, soliciting bribes, and demanding a share of traded goods. As of 4713 AR the Cold Sisters kept an eye on the greedy Ulfen townsfolk of Veshtak, and a number of former mayors, dock wardens, and warehouse managers hung in cages in the town's main square.⁠

Veshtak's mayor as of 4713 AR was the greedy Vidlof Haradsson. Few know that the dockworker Marina Gnetsky is actually Vidlof's boss. When the Cold Sisters come to town, Marina made sure that Vidlof would be punished instead of her.⁠
29842177:
Flying Alderman

The Flying Alderman is a modest inn on the edge of the Foreign Quarter, serving as a safe house for Pathfinder Society agents. Drock Ovix, the innkeeper, is a Pathfinder himself and allows them to use tunnels beneath the inn that connect directly to the Grand Lodge—a closely guarded secret of the organization. Agents can spend three nights free at the inn, while others must pay two silver pieces, which includes bed, dinner, and breakfast the next day.⁠
30722927:
Highwall Market

The Highwall Market, located near the towering walls of Castle Kintargo in Kintargo's Castle District, serves the inhabitants of the castle by selling supplies such as paper, ink, and other mundane essentials to bureaucrats of all stripes. The market also offers other distractions for the weary workers who frequent it, such as food stalls and masseurs.⁠⁠ A statue of the ancient war hero Tellorus Carmus stands at its center.⁠
31029477:
Tradecross

Tradecross is a small collection of farmhouses and an inn in the Plains territory of Molthune. The town is mainly known for the occasional appearance of the mysterious Tradecross Peddler.⁠
53808287:
Azir

Azir, the capital of Rahadoum and the birthplace of the Laws of Mortality, is a bustling trade port whose appearance has been greatly modified recently.⁠
58158177:
Mount Rinia

Mount Rinia is a 15,000-foot-tall peak in the western Menador Mountains, located in the Archduchy of Menador in Cheliax. It is the Maiestas River's source, and home to orcs, humans, and yrthaks.⁠

The mountain is named for the subject of a Taldan ballad, a noblewoman who flung herself from a mountain to escape an arranged marriage, but sprouted wings and flew away to unknown freedom.⁠
74146707:
Lotheedar

The small town of Lotheedar is the capital of Meratt County in the Tandak Prefecture of Taldor. The settlement is officially administered by Count Bartelby Lotheed, who holds the position of tribune, although he has delegated most responsibilies to his seneschal, Sir Gul Gusairne.⁠
98749647:
Lethaquel

Lethaquel is a site in the eastern hills of the elven nation of Kyonin, halfway between the Fierani Forest and the Sellen River.⁠⁠
101859197:
Summer Grove

Summer Grove, in Nidal's southern Uskwood, is reachable solely in midsummer and absent the rest of the year. This hidden glade exudes beauty and tranquility. Wildflowers and lush grasses thrive beneath fragrant linden and sweet cherry trees. The albino Shades of the Uskwood druids and their spiders have never disrupted this place.⁠

Rastel

The ruined city of Rastel was once a thriving settlement of the now-extinct nation of Rastel. The ruins stand upon the banks of the Upper Korir River, in the Korir Plains in the Mwangi Expanse. In common with all ruins of the Rastel culture, the ruined city of Rastel shows signs of fire, conflict, and cannibalism.⁠

Today, the ruins are home to a small number of cambions of Zenj descent. They carry out the traditional Zenj practice of ancestor worship, and include their fiendish ancestors within this. Among these are a group of fiends the cambions refer to as the Waiting Ones, who they believe are asleep beneath the city.⁠

Bildt

Bildt is one of the largest cities in the relatively sparsely populated Lands of the Linnorm Kings, and is located on the island of Aegos in the Steaming Sea. It is also the capital of the Linnorm Kingdom of Broken Bay.⁠
175452857:
Newt Market

The Newt Market is located in Kintargo's scholastic district of Villegre and serves as both the district's main marketplace and a draw for adventurers. The market is known for selling a surprisingly large amount of rare goods and magic items,⁠⁠ including a wand of greater invisibility.⁠

The Newt Market is maintained by an organiser known as The Newt, a title that changes hands on a regular basis but by 4724 AR had been held for an uncharacteristically long time⁠ by a charismatic gnome alchemist who happily uses bribery and intimidation to protect his interests.⁠

Grayhaven

Grayhaven is a settlement built by House Garess in the Golushkin Mountains in Western Brevoy.⁠⁠⁠⁠
193092517:
Cobb Hollow

Cobb Hollow is one of many halfling ranching collectives forming on the North Plains of Ravounel in the aftermath of the Hellfire Crisis.⁠
196804187:
River Inn

The River Inn is a prominent building in the Sprawl district of Katapesh. It was built in 3748 AR aiming to attract a higher cast of locals and visitors. It is a three-story building made of river stones and mortar with strong timber beams. The lanterns that flank its wide doors are lit with magical flames and the interior is suitable for nobles and rich merchants. Unfortunately rich merchants and nobles were never arrived in the district and the ownership of the River Inn has changed hands many times since its construction. The River Inn is still a magnificent building and has some of the best rooms in the city of Katapesh. Marvius Anquen, the current owner, works hard to keep the inn in good condition. Caravans, laborers, and adventurers are the most common customers. They enjoy having a nice place to stay without actually entering the city. A variety of fresh sea fish or river fish from River Scorpius, caught by Marvius's son Eldron, is always in River Inn's menu.⁠
202488427:
Qintong

Qintong is a city in the hobgoblin nation of Kaoling that features a system of social mobility for its non-hobgoblin residents, a unique program that is controversial among the nation's ruling Council of Nine. It is ruled by Sun Zhen, a member of the Council.⁠
223030437:
Anandari Block

The Anandari Block is a Westgate neighborhood populated mostly by people of vudrani descent, and the architecture and food offered in the area reflect this style. The House Anandari are said to have been companions of Khiben-Sald in the past, and in just three generations, they became a prominent family and now control the entire neighborhood, which is patrolled by their Guild of Spears mercenaries.⁠
225284087:
Travelling Man

The Travelling Man is a tavern located in the Old Korvosa district of Korvosa. The Travelling Man's main claim to fame is that it sits near one of the city's "otyugh plugs", a place where the Korvosan Guard can directly feed the otyugh that live within the Vaults and sewers of the city. Every Oathday the guards open the plug and throw in relatively fresh meat and produce. While this feeding is entertaining, in reality, most of The Travelling Man's patrons are awaiting the rare occasions (normally at least once a year) when one of the otyugh rampages and escapes and the Korvosan Guard has to try and recapture it. Because of this danger, the front wall of The Travelling Man is heavily reinforced and its windows are barred.⁠

261830857:
Mithril Hall

The Mithril Hall is a beautiful, traditional-style structure in Westgate that serves as offices and residences for the bureaucrats and diplomats of the Western Council, which administers the district. It is divided into hexagonal sections, resembling a honeycomb, with each office having a corridor that connects to an interior courtyard with a garden and fountain in the center. While undeniably beautiful, it can be disorienting for visitors. The Hall is open five days a week until sunset and later on weekends, and this schedule has drawn complaints from working-class residents who find it difficult to attend to administrative matters or file complaints during those hours.⁠
265655647:
Padiskar

Padiskar was once known as the Shimmering Jewel of Jalmeray, when it was a city famous both for pleasure and for arcane learning. The Arclords of Nex found a nameless horror in the vaults beneath Old Padiskar, and today the city is reduced to being a community of farmers and fisherfolk. The city rings the ancient ruins, surrounding but never entering them. Whatever awful thing the Arclords released still roams the darkened depths below Padiskar, howling in the blackness.

Unlike many other old ruins, Padiskar has yet to be reclaimed by the Thakur, and the locals whisper that there may be some fell reason for this. Some have even claimed the Arclords released a bound deity which had been transported to the island by Khiben-Sald thousands of years ago.⁠⁠
270223967:
Lurching Mountain

The Lurching Mountain is a towering volcano on Raugsmauda's Reach island in the Shackles. The volcano is the primary source of the yellow-gray clouds that loom over the island. Thick fumes always pour out of its crater at the top of the mountain and roll down its sides. The resulting ash looks rotten and it is unknown what chemical composition could create such a unique and unsettling ash cloud. It is said that the lich Raugsmauda practices her foul magic on the top of the volcano.⁠
271581467:
Delenah

Delenah is one of the numerous massive trading cities that dot the Qadiran region of the Plains of Paresh, but is often overshadowed by the capital of Katheer. It is located along the northernmost limits of the nation along its border with Taldor on the southern banks of the Jalrune River.⁠⁠
294063857:
Szigo's Grove

Szigo's Grove is the home of Szigo, the cannibal warlock of the Grungir Forest, who eats his victims in order to gain power. Many adventurers have attempted to destroy this deranged madman, but Szigo has a sizeable following of violent trolls and other monstrous creatures that Szigo has convinced that he is a god.

Szigo's minions serve him as both hunter-gatherers and guards for the horde of magical treasure he has amassed over the years. The most famous item in this horde is probably the magical sword of Laughing Erik, the hero who supposedly came closest to vanquishing the terrible cannibal.⁠
308152897:
Sarain

Sarain is a small village in the River Kingdom of Pitax, close to the border with Mivon.⁠ Sarain is famous for its vineyards and, before the arrival of Castruccio Irovetti, the Liacenza family had overall control over most of the wine-making business of the area.⁠
310782597:
Gazbilah

Gazbilah is a Qadiran city located in the Northern Zho Mountains area, nestled in the foothills between two different spurs of the Zho Mountains. The Northern Zho Mountains are the poorest region in Qadira and face the neighbouring land of Taldor across the Jalrune River. As such, it is the least hungry for war with their neighbors.⁠
321354547:
Summerglen

Summerglen is a deep-sided canyon in the Linnorm Kingdom of Hagreach whose walls are studded with crystals that seem to capture the warmth of the sun, increasing the canyon's temperature.⁠
328287877:
Price of Freedom

The Price of Freedom is a well-respected fighting school in the Varisian city of Kaer Maga. Located in the tenaciously anti-slavery Bottoms district, the Price of Freedom teaches all those who wish the cruel institution's violent overthrow, or who wish to learn how to defend themselves against slavers. It is currently led by the ex-slave and former Chelaxian army commander, Black Marin, who draws on his many years of street fighting experience. The school teaches defense by any means necessary against the scourge of slavery, and encourages students to exploit every weakness and dirty trick they can imagine. The school is free for residents of the Bottoms, but charges a substantial fee to outsiders.⁠⁠

Habe's Sanatorium

Habe's Sanatorium, formally known as the Saintly Haven of Respite, is south of Sandpoint along Cougar Creek near the Ashen Rise.⁠

Erin Habe used his wealth from years as a mental health and diseases expert in Magnimar to build the sanatorium. To raise funds for upkeep and his research, Habe had taken a silent partner, the elderly Varisian Caizarlu Zerren. Habe employs two cambion brothers, Gortus and Gurnak, as orderlies. Habe maintained a working laboratory where he conducted experiments on his patients that might cross ethical boundaries.⁠⁠

After Caizarlu was brought to justice by adventurers, Erin vowed to redeem himself and run his Sanatorium with the original purpose of helping those most in need.⁠

Moth and Flame

Moth and Flame is one of the most popular taverns in Pangolais, thanks to its shows that use illusions to enhance the experience. The owner of the establishment is Theanor of Nisroch, who, along with Lephalia Silvermoth, the lead dancer, conceal their devotion to Desna in plain sight through the shows and theatricality. They use the tavern as a base of operations to smuggle people in and out of the city, avoiding the watchful eyes of the guards.⁠
347014007:
Mosswater

The River Kingdoms settlement of Mosswater was established as a quiet fishing retreat by an exiled Ustalavic merchant named Artoor Geera. Geera's apothecary discovered a valuable process for making luminous dyes from the unusual glowing plant life of the nearby Glow Water Lake.⁠

In 4664 AR a tribe of merrow moved into the area and slaughtered the inhabitants of the village. The aquatic ogres have driven off all subsequent attempts to re-occupy the site and take advantage of the lucrative dye-making process.⁠

Roslar's Coffer

Roslar's Coffer was a small town located in southwestern Lastwall along the Tourondel River, near the border with the Hold of Belkzen.⁠
368020817:
Zincher's Arena

Zincher's Arena, also known as Zincher Arena,⁠ is a massive stone arena that dominates the Wharf District of Riddleport. It holds brutal contests of strength and combat prowess between slaves, criminals, gladiators, and captured wild creatures. The arena also sometimes holds formal duels between members of Riddleport's elite. Since at least 4708 AR and as of approximately 4718 AR, crimelord Clegg Zincher ran the arena,⁠ although his financial collapse after attempting to exploit a fallen star on the nearby isle of Devil's Elbow in 4708 AR eventually led to his being forced to auction the arena in 4718 AR.⁠⁠
374288977:
Defiant's Garden

Defiant's Garden is the mayoral residence of the city of Magnimar, located in the Vista district directly next to the Seacleft. It is the largest and most impressive home in all the city. Defiant's Garden became the official mayor's residence only with the rise of the decadent Lord-Mayor Haldmeer Grobaras; before Grobaras, the mayor's residence was a humbler place within the city that kept him in touch with the people. Grobaras, however, wanted nothing so humble and took Defiant's Garden, which had previously been a palace for visiting dignitaries, as his personal home. The building itself is closer in scale to a small castle than a manor, at eight stories tall and filled with room after room of salons and lounges all devoted to the mayor's pleasure.⁠
380289217:
Gadbadigat

Gadbadigat is an outlaw city located at the heart of the arid Narhari Desert, one of the most rugged and harsh regions of the Impossible Kingdoms of Vudra. The Bahig River, the desert's largest source of water, disappears into a miles-wide sinkhole around which Gadbadigat is built.⁠
382728357:
Restov

Restov is one of the two largest cities in the fertile region of Rostland in southern Brevoy.⁠⁠ It is known as the Free City of Restov, but it is allied with Brevoy.⁠
386980267:
Forest Elder

The Forest Elder is the oldest tree in all of Andoran and one of the oldest on the continent, with legends saying the entire forest grew up around it. In this clearing stands an enormous tree, larger than any city cathedral, with dark wood and roots that reach dozens of feet deep into the ground. Tatzlwyrms often nest in its branches, and members of the Greenfire Circle consider it a sacred place of pilgrimage.⁠

Council Hall and Gaol Block

The Council Hall and Gaol Block in the city of Katapesh is a walled compound standing atop a low bluff overlooking the Lower City. It was known as Aktep Keep and was the estate of Massein Aktep an extremely wealthy businessman in Katapesh. When he was involved in a huge scandal, in 4701 AR, implicating him for tax evasion, fraud, and murdering of several prominent guildmasters, the Pactmasters seized all of his holdings and turned his expansive personal dungeon into the city's new gaol, where he is currently imprisoned. His estate has been converted into the Council Hall where the city's guildmasters and other officials meet. It is also houses the barracks for the Zephyr Guard.⁠

Gojko

Gojko is a tiny Irriseni village located directly on the border with the Lands of the Linnorm Kings in the province of the Verge.⁠
427638817:
Mines of Deeptreasure

The Deeptreasure Mining Company has a hidden and secret base known as the Mines of Deeptreasure that is located on the edge of the Bandu Hills. The company used indentured xorns, who worked under the company's promises to return them to the Plane of Earth,⁠ to obtain gemstones from the hills that were later sold in the Sargavan capital of Eleder, now known as Anthusis, Vidrian. The xorns were promised a way home once they supplied an unspecified number of gems,⁠ but hobgoblin explorers of the Stone Roads from Oprak who encountered and soon sought to undermine the company around 4721 AR then freed the xorn themselves.⁠
437370067:
Yavipho

The village of Yavipho is a tiny, predominantly gnome settlement in central Katapesh, very similar in nature to Tiven's Reed. It grew up around an oasis stopover for merchants and continues to serve as a place where one can sell almost anything to its curious inhabitants.⁠

Constant harassment by slavers (especially from the kholo population) eventually forced the gnomes to migrate beneath the oasis, where homes and workshops are dug from the rock. Most dwellings have secret escape routes, and the settlement itself is carefully monitored by guards for fear of discovery from hostile outsiders. Few visitors are accepted into the community, and those select few are searched before allowed entry. Paranoia is the price of security.⁠
443932617:
Avenue of the Gods

The Avenue of the Gods is a wide road studded with over a dozen temples and shrines that runs through Almas' East Hill neighborhood. Its spectacular architecture attracts the pious and curious alike who come to visit and admire the former Cathedral of Aroden (now a Pathfinder Society lodge), the Golden Cathedral, the temples of Abadar, Cayden Cailean, Erastil, Pharasma, Shelyn, and Torag, along with smaller chapels to various empyreal lords and other demigods.⁠
450211367:
North Bridge

North Bridge, also known as Longriver Bridge, connects North Point and the neighbourhood of Northgate with mainland Varisia. North Bridge is one of the first sights that many people entering Korvosa see, as it connects Endrin Isle with the rest of Varisia and is one of the city's main entry points.⁠

Mount Gustus

Mount Gustus is a mountain in the Five Kings Mountains located northeast of the Darkmoon Vale near Kykar.⁠⁠⁠ It is one of the tallest peaks in the area at an elevation of 14,806 feet,⁠ and the fearsome red dragon Daralathyxl lairs in the nearby foothills.⁠

Atvan

Atvan is a small, peasant town on Glacier Lake in the Irrisen province of Bleakmarch. It is ruled by Baroness Baelara, whose husband, Gregouri Urvalane, is a notorious womanizer. The couple spend a great deal of time arguing, which is what got them banished to this remote settlement from Whitethrone.⁠

The young women of Atvan who attract Gregouri's amorous attentions became targets of the baroness' extravagant rage. To avoid the baroness's wrath, Vaclav Konstantin proprietor of the Sealskinner Inn, has closed down his brothel and employs only local grandmothers in the inn's common room.⁠

Atvan main business is to provide shelter, food, and entertainment for merchants sailing to and from Whitethrone. It is also well known that Atvan has coveted its neighbor Trezira's ice cleaving monopoly.⁠
487298587:
Port Valen

Port Valen is an Ulfen colony on the Scarred Shores in northeastern Arcadia. It was founded by Linnorm King Ulvass of Kalsgard in -473 AR, who travelled to Arcadia after hearing the call of Valenhall, a place of unending revelry and glory.⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠

Until recently, in the Lands of the Linnorm Kings and the Inner Sea region as a whole, the colony has only been known through stories, which refer to it as Valenhall and paint it as the final spiritual destination for powerful lords and brave warriors, who attempt the lengthy and dangerous journey to the colony at the end of their lives, though the truth is much less glamorous.⁠⁠
488366297:
Ganda-Uj

Ganda-Uj is the treetop lair of the monkey goblins of Mediogalti Island. It consists of precariously balanced bark huts, linked by swaying vines and bridges. Scholars believe that the current site is the fifth lair to bear the name; the other four were accidentally burned down by the fire-loving goblins.⁠

The goblins delight in attacking travellers, using nets and poison darts to take prisoners, who are then presumably sacrificed to whatever demons the goblins worship. It is best to travel through monkey goblin territory in large, well-armed groups.⁠
492597477:
Trunau

Trunau is a small human farming community located just south of the old Hordeline in the Hold of Belkzen. When the orcs breached this defensive border in 4515 AR,⁠ the citizens of the town refused to abandon their land, unlike most of the farmers in the surrounding region. They built wooden palisades and ramparts, surrounding the defenses with pits and stakes, and defended the walls of their town with great ferocity. The orc invaders eventually gave up besieging the town and simply started circumventing it. Those few orcs who trade with the inhabitants began naming the settlement Manhome.⁠ The inhabitants of this town are called 'Trunauans'.⁠

Every able-bodied citizen of Trunau is tasked with defending the town at a moment's notice and is grimly aware that the town is the lone human outpost in a savage land. Children on their twelfth birthday are presented with a hopeknife and shown precisely which arteries to cut should they or their families be taken alive by the orc hordes.⁠
508414057:
Vugorak

Vugorak is a community of werecreatures hidden deep within the Hymbrian Forest on the Galtan bank of the East Sellen River. The community welcomes those who are werecreatures and gives them the opportunity to start a new life in the village.⁠
508775977:
Pale Mountain

The Pale Mountain is located in northwest Katapesh near the junction of the Brazen Peaks and the Barrier Wall. It is avoided by travelers as numerous kholo tribes are active in the area. The Carrion King is the ruler of these tribal worshipers of Rovagug.⁠⁠
510908217:
Dabril

The town of Dabril is located on the Sellen River in the tumultuous nation of Galt, just south of Kallas Lake.⁠ Despite being on the river, the residents rarely work as river traders or fishermen. Instead, the people generally work as gardeners or perfumers, and the town has become known for its immense fields of roses and its manufacture of exotic perfumes.⁠
511058207:
Kibwe

Kibwe is a large, walled city-state of trade and mining with a diverse population of Mwangi peoples and non-humans, situated in the eastern Mwangi Jungle west of the Ndele Gap.⁠⁠⁠⁠
516862207:
El-Shelad

El-Shelad is a small city on the Scorpion Coast of Osirion. It was once just a slave camp housing a part of the hordes of slaves that built Tumen. The city flourished under the Qadiran rulership of the country mainly because of the resulting influx of Keleshites that strengthened its economy.⁠

El-Shelad is a city of fierce political struggle and racial tension. When the first Osirian ruler of the country after 3,000 years of Keleshite rulership, Khemet I, the Forthbringer, installed a loyal governor in El-Shelad, he tried to dissipate the political tension. He allowed the city's ruler to retain the traditional Qadiran title of "wali" but the struggle between the Osirian loyalists and Keleshite sympathizers has never ceased. The city is known for its stormy elections which until recently produced Garundi governors loyal to Sothis. Its current ruler, Sarita Senbi is Keleshite and thus distrusted by Garundi citizens.⁠

Deadbridge

Deadbridge is the capital of the Protectorate of the Black Marquis in the River Kingdoms.⁠

On the winter solstice, unusually large ghostly spiders emerge from the shaft. The farmhouse that surrounds the shaft has long been abandoned.⁠

All members of the Yumyzyl tribe make occasional pilgrimages to Darinkhuur's spirit-lodges, where the nation's largest canoes are built and receive blessings.⁠

Kasai is the capital of the Minkai empire on the continent of Tian Xia. The city was chosen as the capital at the founding of the empire in 6119 IC, succeeding Uddo, the former capital under the Teikoku Shogunate.⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠
588484567:
Thunderscale Warrens

The Thunderscale Warrens are a large network of caves on Mediogalti Island, located less than a day's journey inland of the pirate city of Ilizmagorti. The warrens are home to the Thunderscale tribe, the largest of the island's tribes of kobolds. Numerous rumours about the caves make various claims; some suggest they are a source of gemstone or gold deposits, whilst others suspect they lead deep into the earth and perhaps link to the Darklands.⁠

Willowshore

Shrine of the Failed

Taal Mornat

Approximately six centuries ago, dwarves constructed the ossuary of Taal Mornat especially for the servants of the Cathedral of Magrim in Larrad as well as other faithful servants of the dwarven god. The necropolis lies some twenty miles west of the city in a hidden valley within the peaks of the Five Kings Mountains. Over time, due to the fame of many laid to rest there, the site is now a holy and cultural centre for the dwarven community.⁠
596087067:
Bitter Hollow

Bitter Hollow is a tiny thorp on the banks of Lake Coal in central Varisia. It is home to only a small number of hunters and trappers, as Lake Coal has very poor fishing. The Gator's Nest, Bitter Hollow's only trading post, is located in the center of town. The founders of Bitter Hollow must have had some foresight, as they built the wood and reed walkway known as the Wicker Walk to encourage trade with gnomes of the nearby Sanos Forest. Although trade with the gnomes is not regular, one can find interesting and unusual items for sale at the Gator's Nest from time to time.⁠
598471077:
Grislyfair

The Grislyfair is an attempted amusement park that the Grand Council created in the Precipice Quarter to attract new residents and generate jobs. Most of the performers would be wanderers, thus not exposed to the district's spiritual corruption, and the use of clockworks unafraid of spirits should ensure the park's smooth operation. Due to sabotage by either cultists or smugglers, the construction suffered several accidents and was abandoned. The spirits moved about, enchanting the musical instruments and the carousels that now spin aimlessly, making it a place of eerie amusement. Reclaiming the Grislyfair is one of Wynsal Starborn's priorities for cleansing the district of corruption, as similar public works cannot be undertaken without serving as a constant reminder of past failures.⁠

The city itself is home to many alchemists who use the magical plants of the Forest of Thieves to create particularly potent concoctions.⁠⁠

Wreath of Stars

A fey prince named Allarik built an underground dungeon connecting the entrance to the circle on the surface. When Earthfall occurred, most of the dungeon's residents perished, except for an ankou named Edani, who kills all who enter the dungeon. His reputation spread, and a cabal of cultists camped near the standing stones, considering him a harbinger of destruction.⁠
631858637:
Davarn

The town of Davarn in the southwestern Five Kings Mountains is one of the centers of dwarven culture in the region.⁠⁠
634134667:
Sosulka

Sosulka is a small town on the Marbleflow River in Irriseni province of Wintercrux. It is located between the towns of Veshtak in the south and Iarna in the north.⁠

Battlefield

This Battlefield is littered with the corpses of boggards and xulgaths from the Lady's Cape tribes, who clashed in a decisive battle where the boggards won, though they lost a third of their own. Blacksulfur Pond

Blacksulfer Pond is a still, black pond southwest of Nisroch. No rivers or stream feed into it, no fish or other aquatic life inhabit it, and no plants grow near it.⁠

Opparan Trade Commission

The Opparan Trade Commission is a guildhall established in 4714 AR for the purpose of carrying out commissions that benefit everyone, though a little more for Taldor wouldn't hurt. The Storm Tower is located in a valley in the Tusk Mountains with high hills surrounding it. The area around the valley can be used by any orc hold, and the tower offers a perfect view of the skies, so the Storm-Screamers of Rull often make pilgrimages to the structure from time to time.⁠
676142117:
Darkgate

The Darkgate is a fissure in the Precipice Quarter, created during the earthquake that devastated much of the district. Taking advantage of the situation, the Nailfists moved into the area and keep the threats from below at bay. The gang doesn't do this out of charity, of course; they only allow access to the caverns if they are paid a price.⁠

Zaplava

Zaplava is a little village on Rimeflow River just before reaching Glacier Lake in the Irriseni province of Wintercrux. Few travelers stop at the village, inhabited by as many as seven intermarried families. The miserable superstitious peasants live in fear of the dreaded Frozen Fog to the east. The fog's icy tendrils and the strange horrors that sometimes wander close to the village make the frightened peasants hide in their stone hovels. Arko Arkosson is the mayor of Zaplava.⁠

Todora Navanya, a renowned adventurer in Avistan, comes from this tiny village.⁠

Yan Ulvedro's Fort

Yan Ulvedro's Fort was built in the earliest days of the nation of Xopatl by the Arcadian hero-god Ulvedro to help defend the nation against its enemies. Located high in the Mildanesi Mountains, Yan Ulvedro's Fort was designed to protect Xopatl from the neighbouring Razatlan Empire and assisted on the few occasions when Xopatl was attacked. As the power of Razatlan waned, Yan Ulvedro's Fort gradually became more akin to a monastery, and pilgrims from both Xopatl and neighbouring Innazpa now visit the sages of Yan Ulvedro's Fort to seek wisdom and learn their unique mystical techniques. These sages can help travellers reach enlightenment by temporarily pulling their soul out of their body.⁠
725166057:
Water Gardens of Xerbystes

The Water Gardens of Xerbystes were commissioned by Xerbystes I, the first Qadiran satrap of Osirion in the 16th century AR. Feeling that the delta of the River Sphinx was underutilized, the satrap ordered a complex of gardens and pools to be built on an island, and had it shored up against flooding. The new Keleshite elite frequented the garden, but it was avoided by the Osirians, who felt that the attempt to hold back the river was disrespectful to the water spirits. The river reclaimed the island in the great flood of 1535 AR, killing everyone who was there, and it has never been reoccupied. The island occasionally reemerges, leaving parts of the Gardens high and dry, but they are soon submerged in the Sphinx's floods again.⁠
732405617:
Sureshire Ranch

The Sureshire Ranch is a horse ranch located in the Ligos Prefecture of Taldor with a storied history and national fame.⁠ According to the Sureshire family, the first horse was bred here as a cross between a deer and a unicorn. Fanciful tales aside, the Sureshire Ranch has a millennia-long pedigree of horse breeding, and both the nation's aristocracy and Taldor's military favour its horses. Unlike the hulking brutes of the nearby Stavian Ranches, the horses of Sureshire are agile and quick, more akin to the horses favoured in the neighbouring kingdom of Qadira (whom the Sureshire family claims stole these horses from them).⁠

The last of the Sureshire family died over six centuries ago. As of 4717 AR, the ranch is run by a council of Taldan and halfling families who proudly sponsor the Emperor's Mile, a gruelling horse race across the Ligos Prefecture that the ranch has sponsored for 1,200 years.⁠ Its winner is not only showered in gold but gains access to the Well of Kurgess, a spring whose water enhances any beast of burden that drinks from it.⁠
734672307:
Gurat

Gurat is a citadel-city nestled high in the Southern Zho Mountains. The imposing city clings to the edge of a precarious mountain spire and is home of the Mouthpiece of Gurat, an ancient cyclops who serves as oracle for the emperor of Kelesh.⁠ Visitors are not allowed near the Mouthpiece, who is guarded by a thousand deafened eunuchs.⁠ It is believed that the town is named after one of the Mouthpiece's ancestors.

Gurat is considered a holy place to most Qadirans, and pilgrims visit in search of enlightenment. The settlement itself is relatively small, resting on the smallest and flattest of the Zho Mountains, and is surrounded by an 8-foot wall. Gurati locals, known for their open-fire cooking and their weaving, often sit outside their homes, selling their wares to passersby.⁠

The city also has scholarly colleges, with locals traveling there to engage in philosophical and mystical studies. Students are often seen in the streets, discussing such teachings with crowds and passer-byes. Aside from education and basic trade, specialty carpet weavings are often used for flying carpets⁠⁠ and it is claimed that some of the woven patterns of their carpets hold secret prophesies, if one can find and interpret their own life thread path.⁠

764757797:
Figwort Hollow

Figwort Hollow is a marsh that feeds into the Deepcut River in the Nesmian Plains of Nirmathas. The Foxclaws travel to the marsh every summer to harvest figwort, which can be used either as a poison or medicine. Due to a Nidalese ruin in the marsh, there are rifts to the Netherworld, forcing the Foxclaws to fight off numerous incursions.⁠
771625367:
Primarch's Residence

The Primarch's Residence is surrounded by high stone walls and enormous gardens, possibly the most extensive in the city. It is in this majestic building that the Primarch should reside, though since Lord Gyr's disappearance, the building has fallen into disuse. It was built two millennia ago by one of the city's most tyrannical Primarchs, who forced the mages of the Arcanamirium to create illusory chambers within the grand structure. These chambers would remind the sovereign of places where he could relax and escape the city's clamor. It was this tyranny displayed by the Primarch that led the Arclords of Nex to attack the city during the Conjured Siege, where this Primarch perished. However, his successors lacked the restraint to refrain from using the building, for its allure is too great.⁠

It was here that Gyr was last seen, and Acting Primarch Wynsal Starborn has refused to live there, locking the doors and placing the Starwatch on constant guard. Recently, a group of researchers disappeared after a joint expedition between Starwatch and the Pathfinder Society, and the divinations of Third Law Lord Utgar of Gyr have revealed that something is amiss with the illusions placed in the building, leading to theories that it has to do with their connections to the Crux of Nex.⁠
776453477:
Frembrudd

The town of Frembrudd is located on the south-western cliffs of the island of Battlewall in the Linnorm Kingdom of the Ironbound Islands.⁠
793724067:
Citadel Altaerein

Citadel Altaerein is the abandoned former headquarters of the Hellknight Order of the Nail, located in eastern Isger, high in the northwestern Five Kings Mountains, close to the border with Druma. It overlooks the town of Breachill, whose residents call it Hellknight Hill and largely ignore it.⁠⁠⁠
797984027:
Dravod Knock

The muddy fishing town of Dravod Knock is located on the eastern banks of Lake Prophyria in the Kellid nation of Numeria. Across the lake lies the city of Karcau,⁠ but Dravod Knock could not be more different from that cultured, Ustalavic city. Its houses are little more than crude wooden shacks speckled with generations of river silt, while its people make their simple living from fishing the waters of Lake Prophyria, or firing bricks using the copious mud found along its shore. Despite their poverty, the Kellid inhabitants of Dravod Knock are a proud bunch who cling to ancient traditions, many of which seem to revolve around the very mud that seems to be the town's foremost identifier. Countless social occasions are tied to the mud, from how they bury their dead to how they execute their criminals.⁠

Maiaji

Maiaji (pronunciation MY-yee)⁠ was once the southernmost city in the nation of Hongal in Tian Xia. It is now the home to an army of ogres and hill giants, led by the ambitious ettin Nghiem.⁠⁠

Nghiem is known for his love of horse flesh, his short temper, and his unbelievable fecundity. At last count, Nghiem has more than 400 sons and has lost count of his daughters. While Nghiem and Maiaji theoretically swear allegiance to the oni rulers of Chu Ye, in reality Nghiem aspires to build a kingdom of his own and bows to no creature. The ruler of Hongal, Kiriltai Khan, is aware of the threat posed by Nghiem and Maiaji but has proved reluctant, at least so far, to send his own followers to deal with this threat, instead recruiting adventurers to try to deal with the problem.⁠

843450757:
City of Whistling Swords

The City of Whistling Swords is the ruined first capital of the pre-Lung Wa nation of Ootoya, the site of which is now the Successor State of Kwanlai in Tian Xia. This lost city is located in the western foothills of Kwanlai and mostly ignored by its tengu inhabitants.⁠

Still, it draws outsiders and adventurers seeking to loot the city's supposedly untouched armouries, a difficult task since the city is infested with rat kings, oni, and other foul spirits, all led by the hateful underworld dragon Mujihi who was exiled to the surface world that he so despises.⁠⁠
843569057:
Black Whale

Established in 4693 AR, the Black Whale is a prison on the western part of the Flotsam Graveyard intended for the most notorious or politically sensitive prisoners too dangerous to be kept in the Brine in Puddles.⁠

The prison consists of six beached ships, bolted to it with long chains and each lashed together. The guards and other staff stay on the northernmost of the ships, which holds their quarters, all the rowboats, the armory, and the storerooms. An adjacent ship is home to the galley and processing rooms where prisoners are fed and readied for the other ships. A series of pulleys connects ropes and anchors to all six ships, and during rough seas, the prisoners push a pulley axle on each ship to tow supply ships in.⁠

Due to the nature of these criminals, only the Grand Council holds a complete list of who resides within the prison, and few survive long in the squalid conditions aboard (although death typically occurs only due to natural causes). The Lord Warden of the Black Whale is the Fourth Lord of Laws, Guirden of House Gixx. Due to the importance of these prisoners, guards are ever watchful of prisoners breaking out, or outsiders breaking in.⁠⁠

Acting Primarch Wynsal Starborn has proposed overhauling the Black Whale and replacing its leadership due to reports of corruption within the prison; corruption he witnessed firsthand when he was wrongly imprisoned there.⁠

He is said to dwell in his penthouse and conducts all business through proxies, but has never been seen in person. Macini

The Chelaxian port city of Macini, located on northern shores of the Inner Sea in the Archduchy of Longmarch, is located about halfway between the settlements of Hinji and the Corentyn.⁠⁠ It is best known for its prestigious Law Court, to the point that people of Cheliax's southern coast refer to any fair, well-reasoned person as being "sharp as a Macinian magistrate".⁠
1507060897:
Grand Cathedral of Pharasma

The Grand Cathedral of Pharasma in the Varisian city of Korvosa is the headquarters for the clergy of the Lady of Graves, and the largest building in the Gray district.⁠

1524879937:
Kopparberget

Kopparberget is a huge open-pit copper mine located on the northern reaches of the Kodar Mountains in the Linnorm Kingdom of Southmoor. The mine sits at the point where several deep lucrative veins of metals converge. Although the mine has been in operation for many decades, it still provides a great portion of Linnorm Kingdoms' wealth.⁠
1530709727:
Mimere

Mimere is a small town on the eastern bank of the Sellen River in the forest river kingdom of Hymbria. It serves as a trading outpost and boasts a sturdy dock, many small shops, a clean and comfortable inn, and a lively alehouse. River pirates seldom attack the peaceful village, because they have learned that at the smallest threat to the settlement, countless elven warriors descend from the trees, leaving only a few survivors to tell the story. The village has shrines to Calistria, Desna, Gozreh, and Nethys.⁠

Hymbrian elves get along well with their visitors, as long as they stay in the trading outposts. Only elves are permitted beneath the trees of the Northern Hymbrian Forest; others are slain on sight.⁠⁠
1536782497:
District Courthouse

The District Courthouse in the Ivy District is one of the smallest in all of Absalom, having not been expanded for years. Because of this, huge crowds gather outside to watch the trials and performers, of course, take advantage of this opportunity to put on shows that even distract the judges from reaching their verdicts.⁠
1538987937:
Graydirge

Graydirge is a small, remote, and somber ossuary-city in the foothills of the Shattered Range in north-central Geb. The normal custom of Geb is to re-animate its citizens as undead once they die. Graydirge is literally built out of the bones of those Gebbites who were unwilling or unable to be reanimated. Its inhabitants, no doubt, have their own reasons for living in a city-sized ossuary. Its one notable feature is the Empty Threshold, a temple of Zon-Kuthon.⁠ It is home to only one Blood Lord, Berline Haldoli.⁠

Surrounded by a 30-foot wall of fused stone and bone, this city has three main gates to the east, south, and west.
1541402907:
Publican House

The Publican House, also sometimes called the Publican's House, is a tavern and temple of Cayden Cailean located in the River District of Riddleport. It is marked by a dented, gold-lettered sign bearing an ale mug.⁠⁠
1562159737:
Castle Tiapetra

The Castle Tiapetra is a wall fortress on the north-western edge of the Chelaxian city of Corentyn, and features five central towers that all fly the national flag. All buildings of the castle have been converted to stables.⁠

The Castle Tiapetra is one of the famous nine forts of Corentyn, the City of Nine Forts, according to the classical listing.⁠
1604649957:
Blackcove

Blackcove is a small and very isolated fishing village on Ravounel's, formerly Cheliax's, western Hellmouth Gulf.⁠ The ruined island of Nal-Kashel is located two miles off the coast from the village.⁠
1608290357:
Verennie's Lair

Verennie's Lair is an abandoned two-story house with a garden in Rego Cader, Westcrown, chosen by the traitor Ara Verennie of the Hellknights. The place was imbued with her malevolent essence, causing strange effects in the house.⁠
1613518847:
Footprint of the Lost Saint

The Footprint of the Lost Saint is a massive cenote located in the midst of the arid grasslands south of the Mildanesi Mountains in Xopatl. The Footprint of the Lost Saint is believed to have been caused by the death of one of Xopatl's hero gods. Very few who venture to the Footprint of the Lost Saint ever return; those who do tell tales of enormous creatures made of living crystal, and claim the cenote hides a link to the Darklands. Some say the Darklands vault below the Footprint is abandoned, but others claim it is some sort of prison.⁠
1623858287:
Langitheath

Langitheath was once a well-to-do manorial estate in the central Ustalavic province of Ardeal. It and the surrounding 900 acres of farmland were sold by the Loslimor family around ca. 4681 AR, after which the estate passed through a number of different owners before finally being abandoned. Despite the fact that no one is believed to have worked the land for decades, a new crop of flax still grows every year, forming strange spiral shapes around the old manor house. Those who have come close to the estate have reported seeing small figures capering through the fields, or report meeting unnatural children with eyes as cold and blue as the flax flowers of Langitheath.⁠

Ketskerlet

Ketskerlet is the chief township of the Khorkii Clans, built into the Wall of Heaven where the mountains meet the Gulf of Khorkii. The stone halls of Ketskerlet provide shelter for the Erutaki sailors during the cold winter months.⁠ Fully a third of its population is made up of dwarves, who maintain the shelters during the summer.⁠

Zharech

Zharech is a town in western Mendev known for its gladiatorial combat sports.⁠

Grand Pass

The small city of Grand Pass is located on the cusp of the Mildanesi Mountains, next to the pass that links Xopatl with the neighbouring nation of Innazpa. During the height of the Razatlan Empire, Grand Pass was little more than a watch post but, after the empire's fall, the soldiers who once manned the border-post established the city of Grand Pass. Nowadays, Grand Pass is mostly known for being home to the most renowned fighting school in Xopatl. This school holds a biannual tournament that concludes with a spectacular battle atop the nearby Panischo Mountain, the tournament is so well known that it draws combatants from across the whole of Arcadia.⁠
1694863597:
Magilloch Ranch

The Magilloch Ranch is a goat ranch on the Nesmian Plains of Nirmathas. It was originally built by the Magilloch family after the Shining Crusade and has remained in the same hands since then. Unbeknownst at the time, Willow Magilloch, a paladin, was infected by a wasting illness that eventually turned her into a vampire. A few undead-blooded sorcerers appear in the Magilloch family every generation. As of 4717 AR Gran Willow, her family, and vampire spawn created from passing Molthuni soldiers have created a massive tunnel complex beneath their ranch.⁠
1704549627:
Hawah

Hawah is a city in the Ketz Desert of Qadira.⁠
1712543607:
Bloody Tarn

The Bloody Tarn is the base of a tribe of redcaps who serve the Mother of Flies in the Hagwood near Westcrown. Like most of its members, they are violent towards all outsiders, attacking them unless they are invited by their mistress.⁠
1725070097:
Surtse

Surtse is the westernmost town in Almhult.⁠ It is located on the southern coast of Cape Almhult on the shores of the Steaming Sea, to the west of Asre. It lies in the shadow of the Hellrung Mountains further west.⁠
1727757647:
Kaddodi

Kaddodi is a ruined Ghol-Gan city that lies within the Kaava Lands region of the Mwangi Expanse just north of the Oubinga River. The brutal religious practices of the ancient Ghol-Gan civilization as it collapsed has made its ruins particularly attractive to the god-loathing asura. Kaddodi is home to one such asura, Parveen, who was imprisoned within the city by Jatembe's Ten Magic Warriors, but over the millennia the wards holding Parveen have weakened substantially.⁠
1730787377:
Mount Carissa

Mount Carissa is the seventh-tallest peak of the Five Kings Range at 15,126 feet.⁠ It is one of four mountains surrounding the city of Taggoret, alongside Mount Onik to its east, Mount Langley to its north, and Mount Soryu to its west.⁠⁠
1738663597:
Mundatei

Found in a desolate valley at the foot of the Mindspin Mountains in north-eastern Varisia,⁠ the Obelisk Forest of Mundatei is a ruin from the time of the Thassilonian empire⁠ and was built with the labor of enslaved rune and stone giants.⁠ Thousands of ten-foot-high stones, some carved with runes, are scattered about the landscape, and it has long been rumored that they are hollow and hold treasure. A century ago, an expedition from Korvosa tried to confirm this by breaking open some of them. They found that the obelisks were indeed hollow, each holding the desiccated body of a human who had died in terror and horrific pain. According to the Korvosan survivors, they were assaulted by strange undead that night who dragged off a dozen of their companions. The next morning it was discovered that the broken obelisks had wholly reformed. The site has been avoided ever since.⁠⁠⁠
1741287607:
Eastgate Hall

Eastgate Hall is an ornate stone structure that once served a group of adventurers fighting against the corruption spread by Rovagug's followers. Today, it is used by the Eastgate Council, which meets monthly to resolve issues arising in the district.⁠
1753247777:
Immaculate Repository

The Immaculate Repository is a highly visible temple of Abadar in the Dawn Gate district of Katapesh. It is packed with merchant stalls and tents, each of which hangs a decorative key in the front as homage to the Master of the First Vault. They also keep a tithe box, into which customers are expected to drop spare change following a transaction, and from which the clergy collects to fund the daily routines of the temple. Interestingly, none of the merchants take security precautions against theft from the tithe, as few would be foolish enough to rob a tithe box of Abadar in Katapesh, the city of merchants.
1755884947:
Bezin Hall

Bezin Hall once served as a school and orphanage dedicated to educating the community, but it was closed after its headmaster, Satriel Bezin, was executed following the discovery that they had abandoned their faith in the Midnight Lord.
1768699347:
Nagisa

Nagisa is a ruined city on the eastern part of the Bdonge River in the Mwangi Expanse. It is also known as the White City, as its buildings—a number of terraced pyramids, surrounded by smaller structures—are built entirely from white stone.⁠
1779482937:
Husanah

Husanah is a Qadiran city in the Meraz Desert, the barren region that separates Qadira from the rest of the Empire of Kelesh. The Meraz Desert once used to be fertile land before it was sapped of life by the Heralds of Dust. Husanah is located along the coastline where the desert meets the Obari Ocean and is the southernmost city in Qadira. The city of Heger is the nearest large settlement and located north-west along the coastline.⁠⁠
1796296947:
Lenyenko Dark

The cavernous failed mine in the Icerime Peaks of Brevoy known as the Lenyenko Dark leads to a pre-Earthfall complex that dates to Koloran, the ancient cyclopean empire of Casmaron. After a series of unfortunate events, the complex was sealed by the Brevic government around 4639 AR.⁠
1798526307:
Feaster's Dint

Feaster's Dint is a geothermal energy zone near the Wolfrun Hills where a clan of 20 magmin resides. The skittish creatures are not usually a problem for explorers in the region, but it should be noted that they infrequently attack those who enter their territory, and the guards of the settlements in the area consider them a potential threat.⁠
1810887307:
Nesya

Nesya is the capital of the nation of Thieron located on the northern Kardaji Bay coast of the country.⁠

Gujaraldi

Gujaraldi, the capital of Xopatl, is located in the central part of the country.⁠
1836746607:
Saad

Saad is a small town in the River Kingdoms region controlled by Daggermark, and home to Daggermark's cavalry.

The hamelt's two dozen large timber buildings are protected by a motte-and-bailey wall, with several tall timber towers that overlook the surrounding plains. Outside of the wall are many well-guarded horse farms. All of these war-horses are the interbred stock of Yenchabur stallions brought to the area in 4402 AR.

Saad is also the main trading center for the merchant traffic coming from Tymon, and is often the target of bandits who plague all trade routes across the region.⁠

1840384217:
Lahayusa

Lahayasa or Lahuyasa is one of the most important ports in Valash Raj thanks to its trade monopoly with Minata. It was conquered by Kasa Vara's mother in 4694 AR, and although its leader, Raha Sultana, appears to be a mere hedonist, she is a born queen with a shrewd administration and is beloved by her people. She is also very reluctant to relinquish her authority to the central government, and while she doesn't rebel, she tries to ignore as many commands as possible, thus giving the city its own distinct identity.⁠
1844581197:
Hanpa

Hanpa is a town in the Ketz Desert of Qadira.⁠
1849716447:
Bug Harbor

The town of Bug Harbor is a gathering of huts perched on stilts at the edge of swamp Evergrowth. It got its name from the swarms of dragonflies, water striders, and other insects that buzz over the swamp. The town supplies herbs and plants for alchemists, herbalists, wizards, and druids who travel here in search of rare components. The unofficial mayor of Bug Harbor is the aiuvarin Bastin Irriden.⁠⁠
1851001837:
University of Korvosa

The University of Korvosa is located at the University ward of the Heights District of Korvosa. The University provides mundane higher education and holds a great reputation, but not as much as the more prestigious Acadamae. Lady Jessa Leroung founded the University of Korvosa in 4488 AR.⁠⁠

The University of Korvosa consists of five major buildings in its main campus, as well as three satellite buildings nearby and two more in other wards. Its five major buildings are the Leroung Hall, the Black Hall, the Jeggare Library, the Instructor Offices North, and the Instructor Offices South.⁠

The lovely Lady Eliasia Leroung is the current headmistress of the University of Korvosa. She maintains good relationships with most other noble houses.⁠
1853742987:
Corvischior

Corvischior, sometimes spelt Corvischoir, is located in the south of the Ustalavic county of Varno.⁠ The town is now a shadow of its former self, the derelict county capital, and sits across the water from the equally forlorn Castle Corvischior, once the residence of the noble Tiriac family. Though still technically subject to the absentee Lord Ristomaur Tiriac, it has sat fallow for decades, though rumours speak of strange lights and unnerving shadows up at the castle. The most pessimistic residents whisper that Castle Corvischior, once known as Korsinoria Palace, is cursed, and whatever fell hex hangs over the castle has now settled over Corvischior as well.⁠
1856122257:
Wandering Monster

The Wandering Monster is an irregular park maintained by the Ivy District's leshy population. It features an open-air amphitheater that circumvents the rules prohibiting unregistered artists outside the Street Performers and Actors' Guild from performing. It is therefore popular with traveling artists who enjoy nature, and because the Nomarch keeps a watchful eye on who performs here, artists often wear masks to conceal their identities. The Thistleguard used to patrol the area, removing anyone attempting to get on stage, but now the Brotherhood of Abadar maintains at least one member on site at all times to prevent people from being removed unless they actually break the law.⁠
1856298237:
Blood Circus

The Blood Circus is Ilizmagorti's premier gladiatorial combat arena, offering the bloody entertainment so sought after by the city's pirates and thugs. Overseer Saynak is the champion and manager, and the arena also features races and monster battles, among other activities.⁠
1856492127:
Orost

Orost is a trade town of increasing importance in Iobaria. Founded in 780 AR, Orost is the only safe stop on the roads between Mirnbay and Orlov, and thus a site of great importance to the various factions vying for control of Iobaria. Envoys and diplomats from Mirnbay, Orlov, Kridorn, and Veka frequent the town alongside those seeking goods, and local law enforcement is forced to protect local citizens from the intrigue and battles these visitors bring.

At the centre of Orost stands a massive wood and stone building that houses the current komar. The temple is a human construct built over a massive, ancient stone temple. The mosaics on the floor of this temple feature stars, and while the town and its fortifications have taken on a rough star shape over the years, it is from these mosaics that Orost gets its name.⁠
1857344637:
Gerduhm

Gerduhm is an extremely secret dwarven fortress located high in the Tusk Mountains of the Hold of Belkzen, approximately 50 miles north of the Cenotaph. It is operated by the Oathkeepers, a society of dwarven priests of Kols who help maintain an ancient bloodline.⁠
1864568467:
Albatross

The small, coastal fishing town of Albatross perches precariously on a cliffside off the coast of Nidal on Conqueror's Bay. Although it is a settlement of less than 400 souls, it is home to many times that number of its namesake avians. Residents of Albatross claim to be able to predict the weather, foretell ill omens, and see the approach of death simply by observing and interpreting the flights of these birds.⁠
1866748887:
Hajoth Hakados

The small trade city of Hajoth Hakados can be found on the Seven Tears River and was often the first settlement Mendevian Crusaders visited in Numeria on their way north to the Worldwound before its closure. Because of this, it seemed more like a city in the nearby River Kingdoms than a true Numerian settlement.⁠
1866957827:
Little Inner Sea

Little Inner Sea is a neighborhood in The Puddles where members of the Salvage Guild meet in a completely flooded area. It was once a public park, but the saltwater hasn't been kind to the trees. Although scavenging is one of the few legal professions in the district, the taxes levied by Nomarch Haigen Topkick mean that little profit can be made.⁠ Those who can't afford it have to go out at night, with the inherent dangers, as strange creatures fill the lake and the wounds common in this type of work easily become infected. The shops around the lake are among the best-maintained and busiest in the district.⁠
1871453007:
Hostel Sepet

The Hostel Sepet is a keep at the top of Sepet Pass on the trade route between El-Fatar and Ipeq in Osirion. It is built on top of an ancient Osirian fortifications on the eastern edge of the saddle of the mountain. It is surrounded by thick stone walls that rise up several stories. The ruined keep has been sealed up tightly, with only one heavily fortified gate and the narrowest of windows. The inside of the keep is a paradise of fountains and flowers. Hostel Sepet is the absolutely safe harbor for the caravans perilously journeying across the Brazen Peaks with kholo raiders and dangerous wildlife plaguing the journey the entire way.⁠

1890369927:
Xin-Gastash

Xin-Gastash was the capital of the Thassilonian Realm of Gluttony, and was destroyed by the great event that brought down the rest of the kingdom: Earthfall. Constructed underground so that the necromancers of Gastash could practice their arts without the detrimental interference of the sun, Xin-Gastash was said to have contained Thassilon's greatest bathhouses, drug dens, and feast halls. Though much of the city was destroyed and sealed off from outside contact by the earthquakes that shook Golarion following Earthfall, an obstructed entrance to Xin-Gastash exists beneath the mountain the orcs of Belkzen call the Sleeper.⁠
1890824237:
Ash Hollow

Ash Hollow is a small mining village in the foothills of the Mindspin Mountains in northeastern Nidal. It is known for being the primary supplier of coal for Pangolais, and for its annual Festival of Night's Return, held on the nearby mountain of Aghor Thal.⁠
1893494247:
Vhunsaub

Vhunsaub is thought to be an ancient underwater treasury of the Ghol-Gan, and is located among the Cannibal Isles of the Shackles. Many have tried to explore the ruin, but none have progressed past the entrance guarded by a magically compelled sea serpent.⁠
1894488977:
Broken Shield Castle

Broken Shield Castle is a small, isolated castle deep in the Mindspin Mountains of western Molthune, within its Umbral Basin province. Built at some point between 4714 AR and 4717 AR by Captain Breanth Aliskel after her retirement from the Imperial Army, it now hosts a small but growing force of bandits and mercenaries under her command.⁠
1899658267:
Alstone

Alstone is a fishing and farming village located on Flintyreach in the Ironbound Islands of the Lands of the Linnorm Kings. Alstone also has a nearby quarry.⁠⁠⁠
1899871517:
Gray Observatory

The Gray Observatory is a public venue where astronomers from across the nation and abroad gather to discuss their stargazing findings. The building sits atop a high hill, away from the nighttime light pollution.⁠
1905046657:
Aerie of Bloodletting Songs

The plateau known as the Aerie of Bloodletting Songs stands 200 feet above the floor of the Mwangi Jungle. It was once the holy site of an now-extinct tribe of demon-worshipers. The death and suffering which took place here has warped the local animals and forest spirits, which the local Zenj tribes believe are manifestations of the trapped souls of those who died here so long ago.⁠
1941790687:
Graul Homestead

Graul Homestead is a farm in the Kreegwood run by the Graul family of ogrekins. Having blood ties to the Kreeg of Hook Mountain, ogrekin predation rarely extends beyond the forest, though hunters and trappers who venture in often disappear within its boundaries. In 4707 AR, adventurers infiltrated the farm to rescue members of the Order of the Black Arrows that were captured by the ogrekins.⁠

Blisterwell

The settlement of Blisterwell was once an extensive dwarven quarry and strip mine, called Jerengoff, that fell under orc control in -3709 AR with the coming of the warlord Belkzen. It has stayed in orc hands ever since, but is now a hotly contested urban battleground between two orc holds: the Haskodars and the One Eyes.⁠⁠⁠
1953018657:
Lair of Fafnheir

Dread Fafnheir is said to be the mightiest and oldest linnorm in the Lands of the Linnorm Kings, and he has existed for as long as the Linnorm Kingdoms themselves. The Lair of Fafnheir is located deep in the Grungir Forest.⁠ A legend exists that whoever slays Fafnheir will become king of all the Ulfen, and unite the squabbling kingdoms into a single nation.⁠

Steirwood

The Steirwood is a small rotting forest on the Raugsmauda's Reach island in the Shackles. The forest was once home to many animals but now hosts the majority of the hordes of undead that aimlessly roam the island. Raugsmauda creates her necromantic horrors using victims she captures on her monthly hunts. Some of the terrible creatures that wander Steirwood resemble animals that perhaps once populated the isle or distant lands, including bovine ghasts, elephantine skeletons, and serpentine ghouls. The winding tainted trees spontaneously animate their barbed roots to gore and consume zombie animals that wander too close.⁠
1961400677:
Devil's Own

The Devil's Own is a shipyard in the Docks district of the city of Absalom. The shipyard specializes in war galleys used by Absalom's navy and sold to the markets throughout the Inner Sea. Its owner, Lord Archych of House Dureanz is a loyal Chelaxian. He employs the worst thugs and pushes around his considerable weight at every opportunity. The machinations of Lord Archych and those of his rival Goodmiss Alidane of House Candren, manager of the Sea King Shipyard, are the main source of intrigue and violence in the Docks.⁠⁠
1964637117:
Heliu's Folly

Heliu's Folly was one of the westernmost fortresses of the defensive line known as the Sunwall in the Hold of Belkzen.⁠
1976745627:
Katrivish

Katrivish is a small town in Iobaria's Norinor forest inhabited by seemingly mad druids who worship the cyclops god Prathos, and hunt those who trespass in the woods around their home.⁠

Jolizpan

1991969007:
Tumen

Tumen was once Osirion's largest city and briefly its capital. Located 75 miles from Sothis in the eastern Underdunes far from the River Sphinx, the city relied upon pure water drawn forth "by the grace of the Opaline Satrap whom the Radiant Pharaoh had favored, and in turn was favored by", which contemporary Osirionologists speculate, referred to a massive aquifer or portal to the elemental planes. The city's water supply began to ebb shortly before the deaths of the Four Pharaohs of Ascension, and the city descended to abandonment and an endless cycle of burial in the khamsin sandstorms.⁠ The lifeblood of the city was the geyser that erupted from a vertical crater in the mountain, providing its inhabitants with drinking water. The pharaohs used a figurine-shaped artifact, imbued with magic, to make the geyser erupt, though it became inactive after their deaths. The artifact possesses its own consciousness, and if it were to be reactivated, it could once again make life easier in the ruined city, though it would likely begin plotting its own schemes now that its masters are gone.⁠

Despite its remote location, the city remains a popular destination for scholars and treasure hunters.⁠
2008018837:
Ledenica

Ledenica is a small, yet busy town on the Marbleflow River in the Irriseni capital province of Thronehold. The town is fortified against the wintry terrors originating in the Frozen Fog across the river.⁠

Baroness Helka is the efficient ruler of the town and her stone keep is located in the center of Ledenica. The Baroness, convinced by her Jadwiga guard captain Vlad Omelinsky, hires mercenaries to deal with the threats from the Frozen Fog, rather than risk her soldiers. Vlad Omelinsky handles the contracts with the mercenaries and is notorious for cheating and filling his own coffers. The Baroness knows nothing about this and, if she were ever made aware, she would execute her captain.⁠

Ledenica is famous for three of its inns: Natalya's Riverside Inn, the Spirit's Caress and the White Raven. The travellers to and from Whitethrone enjoy visiting these inns. The White Raven is owned and run by sisters Kira Brodovsky and Kaleena Brodovsky and is a secret meeting place for the underground anti-government movement called the Heralds of Summer's Return.⁠
2027421367:
Valahuv

As of 4713 AR, Valahuv was a tiny town in Sarkoris that had resisted the invading demonic hordes of the Worldwound for over a century. Unfortunately, it drew the strength for its independence from its daemonic overlord Ommors, the Bringer of Twilight, who was worshiped as a goddess.⁠⁠
2028934157:
Silver Spindle

The Silver Spindle, formerly known as The Devil's Threads, is one of the many tailor's shops located adjacent to the Redroof Market in the Redroof district of Kintargo.
2029585147:
Khoka

Khoka is a town in north-eastern Qadira on the southern banks of the Pashman River. It is the last stop within Qadira for merchants traveling eastward into the heart of the Empire of Kelesh, and the first way station for caravans entering the satrapy. Khoka is often full of caravans and mercenaries, many bargains take place in the town, and there are more rumors than could fill a hundred ears.⁠

Khoka's permanent population is small, only 920 people,⁠ and residence permits are rarely granted. It is adjacent to a garrison for the Keleshite Imperial Forces, which enforces customs taxation under the command of Captain Jathbiyyah al-Istiyaz. It also contains a temple to Falayna.⁠

Khoka is surrounded by a smattering of small villages in the foothills of the Zho Mountains, including the ratfolk village of Khurbresh located in a canyon less than a day's travel away. The former way station Pilgrim's Rest, a temple to Sarenrae abandoned due to an earthquake-induced shift in the nearby river, is located on the old road between them.⁠

Caravans arriving from the Golden Path east of the town sometimes bring in travelers with a mysterious ailment that causes them to speak in tongues and their eyes to glow bright blue.⁠

Slaves who are particularly devout worshipers of good-aligned deities fetch top coin in Khoka. The slaves are taken from town to the banks of the Pashman River and never seen again. They are destined for Nar-Voth, where they are part of the plans of the archdevil Moloch.⁠

Archheathen's Garrison

Archheathen's Garrison is a fortress in north Corentyn that contains a cluster of offices and civil administration buildings. The basements of the buildings contain secret tunnels leading to safe houses in the eastern part of the Noble Quarter.⁠

Archheathen's Garrison is one of the nine famous forts of Corentyn, the City of Nine Forts, according to the classical listing.⁠

Frostbreach

Frostbreach is a small but self-sufficient town in the northern Lands of the Linnorm Kings, on the Path of Aganhei. Once a more prosperous settlement, its population has since shrunk to about a third of its peak.⁠ It was the site of the Jarlsblood Witch Trial in centuries past, in which the prospective Linnorm King Kolvi killed the reigning Alvard the Wolf in claimed self-defense, but was accused of being an Irriseni witch and executed.⁠

Vannarak

Vannarak is one of the many cities of the naga empire of Nagajor,⁠ and is located in its far western reaches on the nation's northernmost island. A relatively new city, it is built around and within the remains of a massive beached kaiju; its residents mine valuable materials from the beast's remains, and academics and wizards travel to study still-unexplored parts of the corpse.⁠

Fort Serenko

Fort Serenko is an abandoned wooden fortification formerly used to defend the southern border of Rostland in Brevoy. It is located along the Shrike River, upriver from the Crooked Falls.⁠⁠

2116905927:
Kerad

Kerad is a small peasant community on the Rimeflow River in Irrisen's Bleakmarch province. It has little to recommend it, and is often referred to as "Poor Little Kerad" by locals.⁠

Between the sprawling Morozny to the east and the Zelen to the west, Kerad has little to offer to the merchants and travelers of the Rimeflow River. A simple inn and a small drinking house are its only attractions. No Jadwiga has been sent to govern the Poor Little Kerad and the townsfolk, mostly fur trappers and fishermen, are happy for this. Kerad's trappers sail down the river to sell their goods in Zelen. The town elects its mayor every ten years and the current mayor is Anichka Labacova.⁠

Anichka and a number of the townsfolk are in fact members of the underground resistance organization called Heralds of Summer's Return and meetings of the Heralds are not uncommon in Kerad. A carefully hidden shrine of Desna is tended by the priest Dusana Rivanov. Fugitives from the White Witches or other arms of Irrisen's law often find shelter in Kerad.⁠
2118426257:
Saraby

Saraby is a small town on the Thundering River in the Irriseni province of Wintercrux. It is a bustling peasant town which accepts a number of Varisian merchants that have the courage to travel the few treacherous passes across the Kodar Mountains into Irrisen. The brave merchants mainly deliver grain and foodstuff and are richly rewarded. Saraby is ruled by Baroness Zoja who carefully accounts the volumes of trading goods moving through her town. Much of the precious cargo moves on to Dalun to the west and eventually is delivered to the militant settlements and camps of the Verge. The rest, however, is sent east along a route known as the Saraby Trail.⁠

The Saraby Trail to the east follows no visible roads. It follows the Thundering River until reaching the Kodar Mountains and then heads north towards Hope Lost. From Hope Lost some experienced groups head directly east to Sosulka fighting the beasts of the tundra and the fearful white-furred perytons that prowl the skies but most of the groups take one of the well traveled roads that meander through the Skala Foothills to Zlatomesto. There they join a heavily guarded caravan of ore and travel to Veshtak. Bendiks Poljarny and Velna Elishky are veterans of the Saraby Trail.⁠
2125429477:
Temples of Pharaoh Ahn

The Temples of Pharaoh Ahn is a site in southeastern Osirion located between the Salt Hills and the Brazen Peaks⁠ from the brief reign of Pharaoh Ahn, who ruled after the Naga Pharaoh. Pharaoh Ahn believed himself to be as powerful as the mortal Nethys, to such a point that he was nearly driven insane. He ordered slaves and followers to this site in the Brazen Peaks in search of what his advisors told him might be the means used by Nethys to ascend to godhood.⁠

While Pharaoh Ahn searched, his followers constructed inverted pyramids out of precious gemstones to serve as the first palace of what they believed would be their deity Ahn, and magically warded the structures from mortal incursions. Neither Pharaoh Ahn nor his followers returned, however, and later expeditions to the site found only bloody trails toward the pyramids.⁠

As of 4714 AR, the site's only active researcher is Ali Ahmendi, who remained based in Sothis and claimed to be a descendant of Pharaoh Ahn's chief advisor. He employs adventurers in his attempts to explore the temples.⁠

2139052197:
Spindlehorn

A Thassilonian relic from ancient times, the Spindlehorn is a fantastically tall structure located in the Wyvern Mountains of central Varisia. Thousands of feet in height, it rises from the shores of the Storval Deep, contradicting all natural laws of architecture and engineering. It is completely featureless except for a winding stair that winds like a corkscrew around its length, terminating in an open platform ten feet in diameter. The view from this platform is easily one of the most terrifying views in all of Golarion.⁠⁠⁠

To most, the purpose of the spire has been lost to time, although it is told that dark-robed figures can be seen ascending, but never descending its heights from time to time.⁠⁠ However, there is an epic poem Jandelay, inscribed at the base of the Spindlehorn, that implies that Jandelay is place of green fields and spires somewhere within the chaos of the Maelstrom, and that a being called the Oliphaunt of Jandelay is Jandelay's eternal guardian.⁠ So, some have surmised that Spindlehorn was constructed as a platform from which one could summon the Oliphaunt of Jandelay and command it while making eye contact with the massive creature.⁠

Shamans of the Shoanti Shundar-Quah hold the Spindlehorn sacred, making pilgrimages there once every ten years to discuss tribal matters of import.⁠ Rumors suggest a powerful being is buried beneath the tower's base, and the site remains a powerful point for summoning monstrously large fiends.⁠
